title: Copilot review workflow holds only pull-requests: write; write scope for marking ready lives in the app-token job
answers: why does copilot-review.yml have no contents write permission
where to add write permission for marking a PR ready
least privilege permissions for pull_request_target Copilot workflows
which job grants permissions for the Copilot publish step
body:
Convention: copilot-review.yml sets top-level `permissions: {}` and grants only `pull-requests: write` on the request-review job. contents: write was removed from it.
The draft-to-ready step (`gh pr ready`) moved to copilot-agent.yml:publish-draft. That job also sets `permissions: {}` and gets its write scopes from the GitHub App token passed in GH_TOKEN.
Place new write scopes for the publish step in the app-token inputs, not in copilot-review.yml's job permissions.
applies: Permission blocks of the Copilot workflows under .github/workflows that run on pull_request_target.
says: The code review bot should only have permission to update pull requests.
Restrict reviewer automation so it does not have write access to repository contents.
Grant draft publishing credentials to the bot through application tokens instead of pipeline permissions.
Ensure automated assistant workflows adhere to least privilege security for pull request operations.
search: The pull_request_target workflow .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml sets permissions: {} and grants only pull-requests: write on the request-review job, having removed contents: write. Marking draft pull requests ready with gh pr ready runs under copilot-agent.yml:publish-draft, which obtains write access via a GitHub App token in GH_TOKEN rather than job permissions. Any additional write scopes required for the draft publishing step must be placed in the app-token inputs rather than added to copilot-review.yml job permissions.
